questions.q: Which type of malware is designed to execute only when specific conditions are met, such as a certain date or event?
questions.e: A logic bomb stays hidden until a set condition, such as a date, triggers it.

questions.q: What is the primary advantage of using a hash table over a binary search tree for searching?
questions.e: A hash table finds a key in about constant time on average, faster than the log n steps of a binary search tree.

questions.q: Which of the following is a property of a secure cryptographic hash function?
o: It must be dependent on input length
It should produce a fixed-length output
It should allow easy collision generation
questions.e: A hash function turns any input into a fixed-length output and cannot be reversed.

questions.q: A firewall that inspects packets at the application layer is known as a:
questions.e: A proxy firewall works at the application layer and inspects the content of the data, not just packet headers.

questions.q: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for encryption and decryption?
questions.e: The Presentation layer (layer 6) handles encryption, compression and data formatting.

questions.q: Which type of cyberattack floods a system with excessive traffic to make it unavailable?
questions.e: A denial-of-service attack floods a system with traffic until real users cannot use it.

questions.q: Which technique is used to prevent SQL injection attacks?
questions.e: Input validation and parameterised queries stop user input from being run as SQL code.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of asymmetric encryption?
questions.e: RSA is asymmetric: it uses a public key and a private key. AES and DES use one shared key, and SHA-256 is a hash.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a Load Balancer in a distributed system?
o: To distribute traffic across multiple servers
questions.e: A load balancer spreads incoming requests across several servers so none is overloaded.

questions.q: Which of the following is a fundamental security principle in system design?
questions.e: Least privilege means giving only the access that is needed, which limits the damage if an account is misused.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a honeypot in cybersecurity?
o: To attract and analyze potential attackers
questions.e: A honeypot is a decoy system that attracts attackers so defenders can study them.

questions.q: What does an Intrusion Detection System (IDS) do?
o: Detects and alerts on suspicious activities
questions.e: An IDS watches traffic and raises alerts about suspicious activity. It does not usually block it (that is an IPS).

questions.q: What is the purpose of a checksum in data transmission?
questions.e: A checksum is a small value calculated from the data. If it does not match at the other end, an error is detected.

questions.q: What does a buffer overflow exploit target in a program?
questions.e: A buffer overflow writes more data than the memory set aside for it and overwrites nearby memory.

questions.q: What does SSL/TLS provide in network communication?
questions.e: SSL/TLS encrypts the data and proves who the server is (authentication).

questions.q: Which protocol is primarily used for secure web communication?
questions.e: HTTPS is HTTP over SSL/TLS, so it is the secure web protocol.

questions.q: Which attack involves intercepting and altering communications between two parties?
questions.e: A man-in-the-middle attack secretly intercepts, and can change, messages between two parties.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of an ethical hacker?
o: To find and fix security vulnerabilities
questions.e: Ethical hackers find weaknesses legally so that they can be fixed.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a digital signature?
o: To verify the authenticity and integrity of a message
questions.e: A digital signature proves who sent a message and that it was not changed.

questions.q: What is the function of a hypervisor in virtualization?
questions.e: A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines on one physical computer.

questions.q: Which hashing algorithm is considered weak due to collision vulnerabilities?
questions.e: MD5 has known collision weaknesses, so it is no longer considered safe.

questions.q: In relational databases, what does ACID stand for?
questions.e: ACID stands for Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability.

questions.q: What does a zero-day vulnerability refer to?
o: A virus that activates on the first day of infection
A security flaw known to attackers but not yet patched
questions.e: A zero-day flaw is exploited before the vendor has a fix.

questions.q: What is the main characteristic of a polymorphic virus?
o: It hides in the operating system
It requires administrator privileges to execute
It changes its code to evade detection
It spreads only through email attachments
questions.e: A polymorphic virus changes its own code each time to avoid detection.

questions.q: What does the "principle of least privilege" recommend?
o: Allowing all users full control over the system
Granting users only the minimum access necessary
questions.e: Least privilege means giving users only the minimum access they need.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a Content Delivery Network (CDN)?
o: To provide faster access to web content by caching data
questions.e: A CDN caches content on servers near users, so pages load faster.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a component of the CIA triad in cybersecurity?
questions.e: The CIA triad is Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability. Authorization is not part of it.

questions.q: In a computer network, what is an "evil twin" attack?
o: A fake Wi-Fi network that mimics a legitimate one
questions.e: An evil twin is a fake Wi-Fi access point that copies a real network's name to trick users.

questions.q: What is a hash function primarily used for in cryptography?
questions.e: Hash functions are used to store passwords as hashes instead of plain text.

questions.q: What is the key purpose of penetration testing?
o: To find and fix security vulnerabilities before attackers exploit them
questions.e: Penetration testing looks for weaknesses before real attackers find them.

questions.q: What is the function of ARP in networking?
o: Resolve IP addresses to MAC addresses
questions.e: ARP finds the MAC address that belongs to an IP address on the local network.

questions.q: What does "salting" do in password security?
o: Adds random data to a password before hashing
questions.e: A salt is random data added before hashing, so equal passwords get different hashes.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a symmetric encryption algorithm?
questions.e: RSA is asymmetric. AES, DES and 3DES are symmetric.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a penetration test?
questions.e: A penetration test looks for weaknesses in a system.

questions.q: Which type of malware encrypts data to extort money?
questions.e: Ransomware encrypts your files and demands money.

questions.q: What is a zero-day vulnerability?
o: A vulnerability exploited before the vendor is aware
A vulnerability discovered and patched on the same day
questions.e: A zero-day vulnerability is exploited before the vendor knows about it.

questions.q: What is the primary benefit of using a CDN?
questions.e: A CDN reduces latency by serving content from a nearby server.

questions.q: What does NAT stand for?
questions.e: NAT stands for Network Address Translation.

questions.q: Which of the following is a hash function?
questions.e: SHA-256 is a hash function. AES and DES are symmetric ciphers and RSA is asymmetric.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a honeypot in network security?
o: Divert attackers to a decoy system
questions.e: A honeypot is a decoy system that draws attackers away from real systems.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common public-key encryption algorithm?
questions.e: RSA is a public-key algorithm. AES, Blowfish and DES are symmetric.

questions.q: What is the primary function of IDS (Intrusion Detection System)?
questions.e: An IDS monitors and logs suspicious activity. Blocking is the job of an IPS.

questions.q: Which type of attack involves intercepting and modifying communication between two parties?
questions.e: A man-in-the-middle attack intercepts and changes messages in transit.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the Domain Name System (DNS)?
o: Resolve domain names to IP addresses
questions.e: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.

questions.q: Which of the following types of attacks is mitigated by HTTPS?
questions.e: HTTPS encrypts traffic, which stops a man-in-the-middle from reading or changing it.

questions.q: What is an example of a multifactor authentication method?
questions.e: Multifactor authentication combines different kinds of proof. A fingerprint (what you are) plus a PIN (what you know) is two kinds.

questions.q: What is a denial-of-service (DoS) attack?
o: Disruption of service by overwhelming the target with traffic
Exploitation of a vulnerability in a system
questions.e: A DoS attack overwhelms a target with traffic so it cannot serve users.

questions.q: What is the purpose of an SSL certificate?
o: Verify the authenticity of a website
questions.e: An SSL certificate encrypts traffic, proves the site's identity and gives a secure connection.

questions.q: In data analysis, what is the purpose of data preprocessing?
o: Clean and transform raw data into a usable format
questions.e: Data preprocessing cleans and prepares raw data for analysis.

questions.q: What does the term "data mining" refer to?
o: Discovering patterns and insights from large datasets
questions.e: Data mining finds patterns in large datasets.

questions.q: What does the acronym "CIA" stand for in cybersecurity?
questions.e: CIA stands for Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability.

questions.q: Which type of malware is designed to replicate itself and spread to other computers?
questions.e: A worm copies itself and spreads to other computers by itself.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a firewall?
o: To monitor and control incoming and outgoing network traffic
questions.e: A firewall monitors and controls network traffic using rules.

questions.q: Which cybersecurity principle ensures that information is not disclosed to unauthorized individuals?
questions.e: Confidentiality keeps information from unauthorised people.

questions.q: What does the term "phishing" refer to in cybersecurity?
o: A technique used to steal personal information through deceptive emails or websites
questions.e: Phishing tricks people with fake emails or websites to steal information.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to encrypt web traffic?
questions.e: SSL/TLS encrypts web traffic.

questions.q: What is a DDoS attack?
o: An attack that aims to make a service unavailable by overwhelming it with traffic from multiple sources
questions.e: A DDoS attack uses many machines to overwhelm a service.

questions.q: Which of the following is a strong password practice?
o: Using a mix of upper and lower case letters, numbers, and symbols
Using the same password for multiple accounts
Using a common word or phrase
questions.e: Strong passwords are long, mix letters, numbers and symbols, and are not reused.

questions.q: What does the acronym "APT" stand for in cybersecurity?
questions.e: APT stands for Advanced Persistent Threat.

questions.q: Which type of malware disguises itself as legitimate software?
questions.e: A Trojan pretends to be useful software.

questions.q: What is social engineering in the context of cybersecurity?
o: The physical protection of hardware and network infrastructure
The manipulation of people into performing actions or divulging confidential information
The use of software to protect against cyber threats
questions.e: Social engineering manipulates people rather than machines.

questions.q: Which of the following is considered a form of multi-factor authentication (MFA)?
questions.e: MFA needs two different kinds of proof, such as a password and a fingerprint.

questions.q: What is ransomware?
o: Malware that collects and sends data from a computer without the user's knowledge
Malware that locks or encrypts files on a computer and demands payment for their release
Malware that replicates itself to spread to other computers
Malware that provides unauthorized access to a computer
questions.e: Ransomware locks or encrypts files and demands payment.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of encryption?
o: To convert readable data into an unreadable format to protect it from unauthorized access
questions.e: Encryption turns readable data into unreadable data to protect it.

questions.q: What does the term "zero-day exploit" refer to?
o: A vulnerability that is exploited before the vendor has issued a patch
A vulnerability that has been known for a long time
An attack that occurs on the first day of the month
questions.e: A zero-day exploit is used before the vendor has released a patch.

questions.q: What is the main function of an intrusion detection system (IDS)?
o: To detect and alert administrators about potential security breaches
To prevent unauthorized access to a network
questions.e: An IDS detects suspicious activity and alerts the administrators.

questions.q: What does "HTTPS" stand for?
questions.e: HTTPS is HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure.

questions.q: Which of the following is a common type of phishing attack?
o: Using a fake website to trick users into entering personal information
Sending a virus as an email attachment
questions.e: Phishing uses fake websites or emails to trick users into giving personal information.

questions.q: What is the primary goal of cybersecurity?
o: To ensure the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information
To provide free access to information
questions.e: Cybersecurity protects confidentiality, integrity and availability.

questions.q: Which of the following is a social engineering attack?
questions.e: Phishing is a social engineering attack because it tricks a person.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a digital certificate in cybersecurity?
o: To verify the authenticity of a website or user
questions.e: A digital certificate proves the identity of a website or a person.

questions.q: Which malware is known for recording keystrokes to steal sensitive information?
questions.e: A keylogger records every key you type.

questions.q: What is the purpose of two-factor authentication (2FA)?
o: To provide an additional layer of security by requiring two forms of verification
questions.e: Two-factor authentication adds a second proof, so a stolen password alone is not enough.

questions.q: What does the acronym "SOC" stand for in cybersecurity?
questions.e: SOC stands for Security Operations Center.

questions.q: What is a honeypot in cybersecurity?
o: A secure storage for sensitive data
A network decoy designed to attract and monitor attackers
questions.e: A honeypot is a decoy that attracts and monitors attackers.

questions.q: Which law governs the protection of health information in the United States?
questions.e: HIPAA protects health information in the United States.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a Virtual Private Network (VPN)?
o: To encrypt and secure data transmitted over a network
questions.e: A VPN encrypts and secures data sent over a network.

questions.q: What is a brute force attack?
o: An attack that uses multiple attempts to guess a password
An attack that encrypts files and demands ransom
An attack that involves sending deceptive emails
An attack that disrupts service by flooding a network with traffic
questions.e: A brute-force attack tries many passwords until one works.

questions.q: What does the acronym "SIEM" stand for?
questions.e: SIEM stands for Security Information and Event Management.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a DMZ in network security?
o: To separate an internal network from an external network
questions.e: A DMZ sits between the internal network and the outside, to host public servers safely.

questions.q: Which device operates at the Physical layer of the OSI model?
questions.e: A hub works at the Physical layer because it only repeats signals.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a VLAN tag in a network packet?
o: To identify the source IP address
To identify the VLAN to which the packet belongs
questions.e: A VLAN tag says which virtual LAN a packet belongs to.

questions.q: Which port number is used by HTTPS?
questions.e: HTTPS uses port 443.

questions.q: What does the acronym VPN stand for in networking?
questions.e: VPN stands for Virtual Private Network.

questions.q: What is the main function of a DHCP server?
questions.e: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically.

questions.q: Which device is used to connect multiple devices within the same network?
questions.e: A switch connects devices inside one network.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a firewall in a network?
o: To translate domain names into IP addresses
To monitor and filter incoming and outgoing network traffic
questions.e: A network firewall monitors and filters traffic.

questions.q: Which device is used to connect a computer to a telephone line for internet access?
questions.e: A modem connects a computer to a telephone or cable line for internet access.

questions.q: What is the main function of DNS?
o: To translate domain names into IP addresses
questions.e: DNS translates domain names into IP addresses.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the ARP protocol?
o: To resolve IP addresses to MAC addresses
questions.e: ARP resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses.

questions.q: Which device operates at the Data Link layer of the OSI model?
questions.e: A switch works at the Data Link layer using MAC addresses.

questions.q: Which layer of the OSI model is responsible for data encryption?
questions.e: The Presentation layer handles encryption.

questions.q: Which protocol is used to securely browse the internet?
questions.e: HTTPS is the secure version of HTTP.

questions.q: What is the purpose of DHCP in a network?
o: To assign IP addresses to devices automatically
questions.e: DHCP assigns IP addresses automatically.

questions.q: Which wireless security protocol is considered the most secure?
questions.e: WPA3 is the newest and strongest Wi-Fi security protocol.

questions.q: What is the purpose of QoS in a network?
questions.e: QoS prioritises important network traffic.

questions.q: In cybersecurity, what does the term "firewall" refer to?
o: A software or hardware device that filters network traffic
A physical barrier to prevent unauthorized access
questions.e: A firewall filters network traffic using rules.

questions.q: Which type of cyber attack involves exploiting human psychology to gain access to confidential information?
questions.e: Phishing exploits human trust to get confidential information.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the command "ping" in networking?
o: Check the reachability of a host on a network
Test the speed of an internet connection
questions.e: ping checks whether a host can be reached.

questions.q: Which type of attack involves exploiting a software vulnerability to gain unauthorized access or control over a system?
questions.e: SQL injection exploits a software flaw to get unauthorised access.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the command "traceroute" in networking?
o: Map the route that packets take across a network
questions.e: traceroute shows the path packets take across the network.

questions.q: What is the role of a Content Management System (CMS) in web development?
o: Creating and updating website content easily
questions.e: A CMS lets people create and update website content easily.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a CDN (Content Delivery Network) in web development?
o: Distributing website content across multiple servers to improve performance
questions.e: A CDN spreads content across servers to improve speed.

questions.q: What is the primary function of a proxy server?
o: Control access to the internet and improve performance
questions.e: A proxy server controls access to the internet and can speed things up by caching.

questions.q: Which type of attack involves overwhelming a system with traffic to disrupt its normal functioning?
questions.e: A denial-of-service attack overwhelms a system with traffic.

questions.q: Which encryption protocol secures data transmission over a wireless network?
questions.e: WPA protects data on a wireless network.

questions.q: In computer networking, what is a MAC address used for?
o: Identifying a device on a network
questions.e: A MAC address identifies a device on its local network.

questions.q: What is a "bug" in software development?
o: An error or flaw in the code
questions.e: A bug is an error or flaw in code.

questions.q: What does the term "DDoS" stand for in cybersecurity?
questions.e: DDoS stands for Distributed Denial of Service.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a CSS (Cascading Style Sheet) framework in web development?
o: To provide a standardized layout and design for web pages
To secure websites from cyber threats
questions.e: A CSS framework gives ready-made layout and styles.

questions.q: In the context of databases, what is ACID?
o: A set of properties to ensure reliable processing of database transactions
questions.e: ACID is the set of properties that make database transactions reliable.

questions.q: What does the term "DNSSEC" stand for in networking?
questions.e: DNSSEC stands for Domain Name System Security Extensions.

questions.q: What is the function of a DNS (Domain Name System)?
o: Resolving domain names to IP addresses
questions.e: DNS resolves domain names to IP addresses.

questions.q: What does the acronym VPN stand for?
questions.e: VPN stands for Virtual Private Network.

questions.q: In cybersecurity, what is phishing?
o: Sending malicious emails to trick individuals into revealing sensitive information
questions.e: Phishing sends fake messages to trick people into giving away sensitive information.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a firewall in network security?
o: To prevent unauthorized access and control data traffic
questions.e: A firewall stops unauthorised access and controls traffic.
